questions.question:
Consider the following expressions:
(i) false
(ii) Q
(iii) true
(iv) [latex]P\vee Q[/latex]
(v) [latex]\neg Q \vee P[/latex]
The number of expressions given above that are logically implied by [latex]P \wedge (P \Rightarrow Q)[/latex] is ________.
questions.explanation:
[latex]P\wedge(P\Rightarrow Q)[/latex] means P is true and Q is true. Check each expression with P = Q = true:
- false False
- Q True, true True, [latex]P\vee Q[/latex] True, [latex]\neg Q\vee P[/latex] True

4 expressions are implied.

Answer: 4

questions.question: Let f(x) be a polynomial and g(x) = f'(x) be its derivative. If the degree of (f(x)+ f(-x)) is 10, then the degree of (g(x)-g(-x)) is ________.
questions.explanation:
[latex]f(x)+f(-x)[/latex] keeps only the even powers of f (times 2). Its degree is 10, so f has an [latex]x^{10}[/latex] term (and no higher even power).

[latex]g(x)-g(-x)[/latex] keeps only the odd powers of g = f'. Even powers of f become odd powers of g: [latex]x^{10}\rightarrow10x^9[/latex] is the highest.

Degree = 9

Answer: 9

questions.question: The minimum number of colours that is sufficient to vertex-colour any planar graph is _________.

By the four colour theorem, every planar graph can be properly coloured with 4 colours, and some (e.g. [latex]K_4[/latex]) need all 4.

Answer: 4

questions.question:
Consider the systems,each consisting of m linear equations in n variables.
I. If m [latex]\lt[/latex] n, then all such systems have a solution
II. If m [latex]\gt[/latex] n, then none of these systems has a solution
III. If m = n, then there exists a system which has a solution
Which one of the following is CORRECT?

options.A: I, II and III are true
options.B: Only II and III are true

questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- I: m [latex]\lt[/latex] n does not guarantee a solution: x + y = 1 and x + y = 2 are inconsistent [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- II: m [latex]\gt[/latex] n systems can have solutions (e.g. the same equation repeated) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- III: with m = n, the homogeneous system Ax = 0 always has x = 0 as a solution [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Only III is true

The probability of an LED bulb lasting more than 100 hours given that it is of Type 1 is 0.7, and given that it is of Type 2 is 0.4. The probability that an LED bulb chosen uniformly at random lasts more than 100 hours is _________.
questions.explanation:
Both types are equally likely (0.5 each). Total probability:
[latex]P=0.5\times0.7+0.5\times0.4=0.35+0.2=0.55[/latex]

questions.question: Consider an eight-bit ripple-carry Combinational Circuit for computing the sum of A and B, where A and B are integers represented in 2's complement form. If the decimal value of  A is one, the decimal value of B that leads to the longest latency for the sum to stabilize is ________.
questions.explanation:
The longest delay happens when a carry is generated at bit 0 and has to ripple through all 8 bits. A = 0000 0001, so B should be all 1s: 1111 1111 = [latex]-[/latex]1.

Answer: -1

questions.question:
Let, [latex]x_{1} \oplus x_{2} \oplus
x_{3} \oplus x_{4}=0[/latex] where [latex]x_{1},  x_{2} ,
x_{3} , x_{4}[/latex]  are Boolean variables, and  [latex]\oplus[/latex] is the XOR operator.
Which one of the following must always be TRUE?
questions.explanation:
[latex]x_1\oplus x_2\oplus x_3\oplus x_4=0\Rightarrow x_1\oplus x_3=x_2\oplus x_4[/latex].

Complementing both inputs of an XOR does not change it ([latex]\bar a\oplus\bar b=a\oplus b[/latex]), so [latex]\bar x_1\oplus\bar x_3=\bar x_2\oplus\bar x_4[/latex] is always true.

The other options fail for x = 1111 (XOR = 0, but the product is 1, and so on).

Answer: Option 3

questions.question:
Assume that the algorithms considered here sort the input sequences in ascending order. If the input is already in ascending order, which of the following are TRUE?
I. Quicksort runs in [latex]\Theta (n^{2})[/latex] time
II. Bubblesort runs in [latex]\Theta (n^{2})[/latex] time
III. Merge sort runs in [latex]\Theta (n)[/latex] time
IV. Insertion sort runs in [latex]\Theta (n)[/latex] time
questions.explanation:
On already sorted input:
- Quicksort (first/last element as pivot) makes the most unbalanced splits [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\Theta(n^2)[/latex] True
- Bubble sort with the "no swap" check stops after one pass [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex] False
- Merge sort is always [latex]\Theta(n\log n)[/latex] False
- Insertion sort compares each element once [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex] True

Answer: I and IV only

questions.question:
N items are stored in a sorted doubly linked list. For a delete operation, a pointer is provided to the record to be deleted. For a decrease-key operation, a pointer is provided to the record on which the operation is to be performed.
An algorithm performs the following operations on the list in this order: [latex]\Theta(N) \; delete [/latex] , [latex] O(logN) \; insert [/latex], [latex] O(logN) \; find [/latex], and [latex] \Theta(N) \; decrease-key[/latex]. What is the time complexity of all these operations put together?
questions.explanation:
In a sorted doubly linked list (pointers given for delete and decrease-key):
- delete: [latex]O(1)[/latex] each [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\Theta(N)[/latex] in total
- insert: find the position, [latex]O(N)[/latex] each [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(N\log N)[/latex]
- find: [latex]O(N)[/latex] each [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(N\log N)[/latex]
- decrease-key: the node may have to move back towards the front, [latex]O(N)[/latex] each [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]O(N^2)[/latex]

Total = [latex]O(N^2)[/latex]

Answer: [latex]O(N^2)[/latex]

questions.question: In which one of the following page replacement algorithms it is possible for the page fault rate to increase even when the number of allocated frames increases?
questions.explanation:
This is Belady's anomaly, which happens with FIFO. LRU, OPT and MRU are stack algorithms: with more frames the set of pages in memory only grows, so faults never increase.

Answer: FIFO

questions.question: B+ Trees are considered BALANCED because

options.C: the number of children of any two non-leaf sibling nodes differ by at most 1
options.D: the number of records in any two leaf nodes differ by at most 1.

In a B+ tree all leaves are always at the same depth (splits and merges happen at the root level), so every root-to-leaf path has the same length.

questions.question: Suppose  a database schedule S involves transactions T1,...,Tn. Construct the precedence graph of S with vertices representing the transactions and edges representing the conflicts. If S is serializable, which one of the following orderings of the vertices of the precedence graph is guaranteed to yield a serial schedule?
questions.explanation:
Each edge [latex]T_i\rightarrow T_j[/latex] means [latex]T_i[/latex] must come first. A serializable schedule has an acyclic precedence graph, and any topological order respects every edge, so it gives an equivalent serial schedule.

The exponential backoff mechanism reduces the probability of collisionon

questions.question: Which one of the following well-formed formulae in predicate calculus is NOT valid?

options.A: [latex](\forall x p(x)\Rightarrow \forall xq(x))\Rightarrow (\exists x\neg p(x) \vee \forall xq(x))[/latex]
options.D: [latex]\forall x (p(x)\vee q(x))\Rightarrow (\forall x p(x) \vee \forall x q(x)) [/latex]

questions.question:
Consider a set U of 23 different compounds in a Chemistry lab. There is a subset S of U of 9 compounds, each of which reacts with exactly 3 compounds of U. Consider the following statements:

I. Each compound in U \ S reacts with an odd number of compounds.
II. At least one compound in U \ S reacts with an odd number of compounds.
III. Each compound in U n S reacts with an even number of compounds.

Which one of the above statements is ALWAYS TRUE?
questions.explanation:
Model compounds as vertices and reactions as edges. The sum of all degrees is even (handshake lemma).

The 9 compounds in S have degree 3 each: total 27 (odd). So the degrees of U \ S must add to an odd number, which needs at least one odd degree there. Nothing forces every one to be odd.

Answer: Only II

questions.question: Suppose the functions F and G can be computed in 5 and 3 nano seconds by functional units [latex]U_{F}[/latex] and [latex]U_{G}[/latex], respectively. Ignoring all other delays, the minimum time required to complete this computation is ________ nanoseconds.
questions.explanation:

F can start only after the first G results are ready (3 ns), and the G units keep feeding F in time after that.

Total = 3 + 25 = 28 ns

Answer: 28

A complete binary min-heap is made by including each integer in [1,1023] exactly once. The depth of a node in the heap is the length of the path from the root of the heap to that node. Thus, the root is at depth 0. The maximum depth at which integer 9 can appear is_____.

If |E|=m and |V|=n, and the memory size is not a constraint, what is the Asymptotic Notation of the most efficient algorithm to set the twin pointer in each entry in each adjacency list?

Go through all edges once (scanning every adjacency list), using an n [latex]\times[/latex] n table (memory is no problem) to remember where entry [v] in u's list is.
